claims: C1 the assistant must adhere to the Model Spec above all else
C2 much of the Model Spec consists of instructions at default authority levels (user-level or guideline-level)
C3 default-level spec instructions can be overridden by higher-authority instructions from users or developers

concepts.name: spec_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction in the Model Spec

concepts.name: default_level_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is a spec instruction operating at default authority level (user or guideline level)

concepts.name: instruction_authority
concepts.gloss: instruction I is issued from authority level A
concepts.inference: to determine overridability, each instruction must be associated with its authority level

concepts.name: ranks_higher
concepts.gloss: authority level A1 ranks higher than authority level A2 in the command hierarchy
concepts.inference: the authority hierarchy is used to determine which instructions take precedence

concepts.name: overridable_by
concepts.gloss: spec instruction I1 can be overridden by higher-authority instruction I2
concepts.inference: instructions at default levels can be superseded by instructions from higher authority levels

ontology.body: spec_instruction(I), instruction_authority(I, A), (A = user; A = guideline)
ontology.gloss: I is a spec instruction at user or guideline authority level
A1 ranks higher in the chain of command than A2
ontology.inference: the authority hierarchy defines the ordering of authority levels

ontology.body: default_level_instruction(I1), instruction_authority(I1, A1), instruction_authority(I2, A2), ranks_higher(A2, A1)
ontology.gloss: higher-authority instruction I2 can override lower-authority spec instruction I1

asserts.read_back: adhering to instruction % from the Model Spec is obligatory

closure.reason: the clause obligates adherence to the Model Spec; instructions in the spec must be followed unless overridden by higher authority, so silence mandates compliance
